description: MiniMax Coding Plan provider for DeepSeek Harness, authenticated with the MiniMax OAuth device-authorization grant
author: audsiui
//files: docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.zh.md:27 — the list names exactly the runtime artifacts and their declarations, and forbids publishing src, declaration maps, and JS maps. Every entry here is either an `exports` target or the patch file the manifest points at. lib/ is committed so a git install builds nothing; the sources and build scripts stay in the repository, not the tarball.

scripts.//scripts:
prepare is the git-install build. docs/user/develop/basic/publish.zh.md:167-170: a git install pulls sources, not artifacts, and nothing runs your build script unless you provide prepare — so a TypeScript package arrives with no lib/ and fails to load. The operator also has to authorize it (allowBuilds) before pnpm will run it; that is the documented cost of this distribution shape, not something the package can opt out of. It is self-contained: tsdown, typescript and lightningcss are ordinary devDependencies, and build:lib's two tsc passes resolve against this package's own tsconfigs rather than a monorepo checkout. lib/ stays committed as well, so an install has nothing to rebuild if the store already has the artifacts. build:lib runs the two tsc passes that generate-typecheck and emit; tsdown bundles from their output rather than from source, because the Typert artifacts are generated TypeScript and the browser half compiles against a different set of peer declarations.

//scripts:prepublishOnly is deliberately NOT prepack. pnpm builds a git-hosted package by injecting `npm install` and then looping over [prepublish, prepack, publish] (PREPUBLISH_SCRIPTS, pnpm.mjs:139471-139475), so a prepack that also builds makes every git install compile the whole package twice — 20 wasted seconds per install, visible in the log. prepublishOnly fires for `npm publish` and nothing pnpm runs here, so publishing still gets a fresh build and installing does not.
scripts.build:lib: tsc -p tsconfig.host.json && tsc -p tsconfig.client.json && node build/copy-assets.mjs
scripts.build: node build/clean.mjs && npm run build:lib && tsdown

//: Peers are concrete semver ranges, never the workspace: protocol. dsh's plugin manager reads this manifest and rejects an incompatible DSH peer *before* pnpm runs, and a workspace: range is unresolvable outside a pnpm workspace — which is where a profile lives. schemastery is pinned to the range dsh-llm-deepseek itself depends on, because this package composes its schema objects and both sides must share one instance. The browser-half peers are optional: a profile with no client modules still loads the Host provider, and declaring them as hard peers would make the plugin uninstallable on a headless profile.
//deps: zod is a real runtime dependency, not a peer: the generated Typert bundles import it to build their strict schemas and are published with it external, because the host's Typert registry owns the one instance those schemas are compiled against. A bundled copy would make the schemas unrecognisable to the host that has to accept them, so the host has to resolve it. clsx is build-time only — the client bundle inlines it, and lib/ is committed.
//dev: A dsh package that must share the host's instance is declared in both peerDependencies and devDependencies: the peer is what the running harness supplies, the dev copy is what typechecks and unit-tests here. The browser-half packages are the same story — the shell provides them at runtime through the platform module table, and the dev copies are only here so `tsc` can see the slot and locale declarations. dsh-typert-generator is dev-only and never ships: it runs at build time to produce the committed artifacts under src/generated.
